hard_failures: unsafe or impossible joint alignment or load path
extra, missing, fused, or malformed limbs, hands, feet, or fingers
wrong, missing, floating, or physically impossible equipment
head, hands, working equipment, knees, or feet leave the frame
camera motion hides setup or working range
BIL wordmark changes spelling, geometry, location, or moves independently
third-party logo, watermark, caption, UI, or duplicated person
synthetic-looking skin, face, fabric, equipment, gravity, or contact
distracting lighting, background, flicker, morphing, or continuity error
review_profile.publication_gate: qualified human biomechanics and rights review required

brand_and_reality_prompt: Photorealistic premium commercial gym, real full-size equipment with believable weight and contact, locked 9:16 full-body camera, natural skin and fabric, accurate hands, feet and joint mechanics. Keep clothing plain and unbranded so no logo can warp with the moving trainer. Show the canonical BIL(TM) wordmark only on two stationary physical surfaces already present in the source image: a fixed rear-wall studio sign and a fixed equipment-base plaque. Both have real depth, perspective, occlusion and contact shadow; neither is an overlay, watermark, tracked patch, HUD, caption or moving object. No third-party marks.

video_duration_policy.reason: Ten seconds reliably shows setup, one complete controlled repetition and return without padding or rushing the movement.

months.progression: Keep 2-4 good repetitions in reserve; learn stable setup and range.
months.deload: Week 4: reduce working sets by about one third.

months.progression: Add repetitions inside the range before adding a small load.
months.deload: Week 8: reduce sets and keep all repetitions comfortably controlled.

months.progression: Continue the rotation across calendar weeks; never cram missed sessions.
months.deload: Final week: one A session per pattern only.

months.progression: Most work uses 8-15 reps with 1-3 repetitions in reserve.
months.deload: Final 5-7 days: half the accessory sets.

months.progression: Primary lifts use the lower end of their range; accessories stay controlled.
months.deload: Final week: no grinding repetitions and reduce primary load.

months.progression: Choose one lagging pattern for one extra accessory set, not every pattern.
months.deload: Week 24: technique-only sessions, then restart with updated loads.
